subject: Request: temporary latency band for Vision-XL pilot (Acme.ai)
messages:
From: Maria Torres <maria.torres@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: GCP Partner <cloud-sre@gcp-partner.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Vision-XL pilot timing & throughput concern

Marcus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning — the Acme AI product team is scheduled to kick off the Vision-XL pilot tomorrow (Dec 5). We started running a small baseline load today and are seeing intermittent p95 latency spikes around 1.0–1.3s for high-resolution frames when we push to 8–12 concurrent inference streams. Baseline target for our app is 400–500ms p95.

We understand this is a preview model and expect some variance, but the pilot timeline is tight: we need consistent experience for a handful of enterprise customers during the first 72 hours. Can Redwood temporarily accept a relaxed latency band for the pilot route (Vision-XL, high-res profile) or route canary traffic to a higher-capacity pool? If possible please share a short mutual action plan so we can sign off internally.

Attaching a short sample of timestamps and traces (we pulled logs on our side).

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Torres
Product, Acme.ai
attachment: acme-traces-sample-20271204.json (json)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Maria Torres <maria.torres@acme.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Vision-XL pilot timing & throughput concern

Hi Maria — appreciate the quick heads up and the traces.

Short answer: yes, we can support a temporary, scoped change for the pilot route. I'll kick off an internal SLA exception request and coordinate canary routing + capacity tweaks. Two asks from our side: (1) confirm the pilot window (hours/dates) and expected QPS per route, (2) allow Redwood to enable additional tracing for the pilot so we can do root-cause quickly.

Proposed interim: raise p95 latency band to 1100–1200ms for the Vision-XL high-res route for a rolling 72-hour window, during which we provision a higher-cost canary pool and enable detailed perf traces. We'll provide a short rollback plan if we see error-rate regressions.

Looping in Mina and Dev to attach capacity/infra recommendations — will follow up with an internal summary and the exceptions ticket.

-Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2027 10:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Vision-XL pilot timing & throughput concern — quick SLO exception request

Team — forwarding Acme's note. Pilot starts Dec 5; they observe p95 spikes 1.0–1.3s on high-res frames. Proposed temporary SLO: p95 <= 1200ms (route-specific) for 72 hours while we provide a canary on higher capacity.

Can you validate feasibility? I know Vision-XL is heavier (longer kv-cache warmups). Key questions:
- Can we provision a dedicated canary pool (short-term) for Acme with higher-spec GPUs?
- Can we enable request-level tracing and keep tracing retention short?
- Any concerns on billing/credits or contract language for the temporary SLO?

I attached the latency snapshot we pulled from our test harness this morning. I'll prepare the exceptions ticket after we confirm the plan.

Thanks,
Marcus
attachment: vision-xl-latency-snapshot-20271204.csv (csv)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2027 13:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vision-XL pilot timing & throughput concern — quick SLO exception request

Marcus / team — quick engineering note after a short replay of Acme traces. TL;DR: feasible with tradeoffs.

What we recommend:
- Provision a short-lived canary pool (48–72h) using two xA100-40g equiv nodes (region: us-west-2) and route Acme's pilot traffic to that pool via a route override. That gives consistent latency headroom.
- Serve a quantized Vision-XL variant (int8 hybrid) for the high-res profile to reduce decode time; expect ~20–30% p95 improvement versus float16.
- Temporarily accept p95 <= 1.1s (1100ms) as the SLO for that route for a rolling 72-hour window. Why 1.1s? It balances shipping the pilot and limiting customer impact; 1.2s feels conservative.
- Enable request tracing (sampling rate 25%) and short-term retention (7d). We will redact PII before storing.

Operational guardrails:
- Auto-fallback: if error-rate > 0.5% or 5xxs spike, route back to baseline model and notify Acme + Redwood on-call (ops escalation).
- Cost: Acme will be billed at Dedicated canary rate; Marcus please confirm if a credits adjustment is needed in the deal.

I created a JIRA for tracking: SUP-8219. I also uploaded a short perf summary to the pilot Drive folder.

Regards,
Dev
Infra / Serving Runtime
attachment: acme-pilot-metrics-summary.pdf (pdf)

Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2027 16:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary latency band for Vision-XL pilot (Acme.ai)

Maria — thanks for the patience while we validated options. Per internal analysis the recommended path is below; Acme team please reply with a quick ACK if this plan matches what you need.

Redwood recommended pilot plan (summary):
- Window: Dec 6 00:00 PST — Dec 9 00:00 PST (72 hours rolling)
- SLO change (route-specific): p95 <= 1100ms for Vision-XL high-res profile
- Capacity: short-lived canary pool (2 xA100-40g equiv) routed via route override
- Model: quantized Vision-XL variant for high-res path (decreased latency, identical output quality baseline tests)
- Observability: request tracing (25% sample), 7-day retention, additional perf dashboards provided to Acme
- Safety: auto-fallback to baseline model if 5xx > 0.5% or error-rate spike; immediate rollback if accuracy regressions detected
- Billing: canary runs billed at Dedicated canary rate. Marcus — will follow up on one-off credits if needed.

Next steps: Acme please ACK the window and we will open formal exceptions ticket (JIRA SUP-8219) and schedule the canary provisioning.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
